question.:question/problem: Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5x-1}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=5x-1.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (5) \\  & =-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{(5x-1{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-{x}^{2}+2x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2-2x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (2-2x) \\  & =-\frac{2(x-1)}{2\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+2x}} \\  & =-\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+2x}}.\end{aligned}

Finally, substituting $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+2x}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2-2(1)}{2\sqrt{-(1{)}^{2}+2(1)}} \\  & =\frac{0}{2\sqrt{1}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{-6x+7}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-6x+7.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-6) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+7}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+7}}-3x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-3} & =-\frac{6}{2\sqrt{-6(-3)+7}}-3(-3)^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}-27 \\  & =-\frac{138}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
